messages:
Alex_Sales: Hey team — customer (EduCloud Inc) is asking to put the Marketplace commit on their central procurement entity (EduCloud-Payables) but legal insists the contract needs to be with a different BU (EduCloud-Platform). They want split billing across two entities and the PO must include specific tax IDs. Can we do a split commit / split invoice on the AWS Marketplace flow? :thinking:

Mara_Procure: short answer: marketplace invoices are generated by the marketplace seller entity. AWS/GCP typically won't emit two separate vendor invoices for a single marketplace subscription. Procurement can accept an invoice for the marketplace seller and then do internal alloc/proration, but tax/tin must match the vendor on the invoice. We need to know which entity is the legal contracting party vs the bill-to.

Jin_Finance: Important: if the customer requires a vendor invoice that lists EduCloud-Platform as vendor (for tax reclaim), marketplace may not work because the marketplace seller entity is our company-level marketplace account. Two options: 1) Use direct contract (non-marketplace) so we can issue invoice to EduCloud-Platform with their TIN; 2) Accept marketplace invoice to EduCloud-Payables and set up intercompany recharges/credit memos. Both have tax and timing implications. Which does the customer prefer?

Sam_Eng: From infra side, nothing technical prevents us from tagging usage to different customer billing identifiers for Dedicated/Private deployments (we can route metering). Hosted/Marketplace is constrained by the marketplace provider's billing model. If they need invoice-level control, recommend Dedicated or Direct order.

Leo_SalesOps: Deal desk flag: splitting a committed discount across two legal entities requires approval. We treat the commit as a single economic commitment; splitting discounts needs a carve-out clause and sign-off from revenue ops. Also need to confirm whether both entities will be on the same rate card / discount tier. Please attach the proposed revenue split percentages.

Alex_Sales: Thanks. Customer says: 60% of usage should land on EduCloud-Platform (contracting BU) and 40% on EduCloud-Payables (procurement). They want a single PO (master PO) that references our marketplace SKU but lists bill-to = EduCloud-Payables and remit-to = EduCloud-Platform (they use internal cost allocation). They also want our vendor tax id to appear next to line items. Is there an approved template for this?

Mara_Procure: We have a minimal template. Key fields they must populate: PO number, bill-to entity name, remit-to entity name, remit-to tax id (TIN/VAT), PO contact + email, funding account code. If marketplace used, market invoice will show our marketplace vendor tax id; you can add the customer's PO number to the invoice reference. If they insist remit-to must be our contract entity, we need direct order.

Jin_Finance: I'll need to loop in tax. If they want VAT reclaim, we need to ensure invoice includes our registered VAT number and a valid invoice address. Marketplace invoices sometimes omit address lines. Please ask customer to confirm whether their AP team will accept marketplace invoice format. If not, escalate to legal for direct order.

ProcureBot: New PO uploaded to /shared/procurements/EduCloud_PO_98765.pdf — link: https://files.internal/redwood/EduCloud_PO_98765.pdf :white_check_mark:

Leo_SalesOps: For the deal desk approval: attach a short memo with (a) why marketplace is required, (b) split percentages, (c) whether the customer will accept marketplace invoice format, (d) proposed revenue recognition notes. I'll triage. Also include the customer's procurement contact and timeline for the PO.

Alex_Sales: Copying the procurement contact: Mara, PO contact is Claire Hu (claire.hu@educloud.com). Timeline: they want the PO processed this week to hit next quarter commit. I'll draft the memo and proposed split. Quick question for Jin — if we end up doing marketplace + internal recharge, can finance auto-generate the credit memo monthly?

Jin_Finance: We can automate recharges but need an SFTP feed or API with line-level usage mapping and cost split rules. Suggested fields for the feed: `invoice_id`, `line_item_id`, `usage_units`, `billing_entity`, `allocation_pct`, `customer_po`. Example payload:

```
{
  "invoice_id": "AWS-INV-2026-0001",
  "line_item_id": "sku-llm-001",
  "usage_units": "12345",
  "billing_entity": "EduCloud-Platform",
  "allocation_pct": "60",
  "customer_po": "PO-98765"
}
```

If they can provide mapping nightly we can run automated credit memos. That needs one-time engineering work to expose the feed.

Sam_Eng: We can produce a nightly CSV export with those fields and push to SFTP. It'll take ~2 sprints to wire up for a new customer (auth + schema + monitoring). If this is blocking the close, recommend short-term: accept a manual monthly file for the first quarter.

Alex_Sales: Great — I'll propose (A) short-term: marketplace billing to EduCloud-Payables + monthly manual allocation file, (B) medium-term: automated SFTP feed + credit memos, (C) long-term: move to direct contract if procurement refuses marketplace format. I'll attach the memo in 30m. Thanks! :thumbsup:

Mara_Procure: Thanks Alex — once the memo is attached I'll start procurement checklist. If they need our VAT and remit address, use this: `Vendor Name: Redwood Inference, VAT: 12-3456789, Invoice Address: 123 Runtime Ave, Palo Alto, CA 94301`. Confirm with legal before sharing outbound. :wave:
